title: Model Migration & Cutover Governance: telemetry contracts, safety gates, and SLA carveouts
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Summary:
This playbook defines the governance, telemetry contracts, safety gates, and SLA carveouts for enterprise model migrations and cutovers. It is intended for Customer Success (CS), SRE, Product, and Security stakeholders who jointly own customer-facing model upgrades or tenant re-allocations (hosted, dedicated, or private).

Why this exists:
- Model migrations change output fidelity, token cost, and performance characteristics. Customers expect minimal disruption and an auditable trail for decisions that affect SLA eligibility and service credits.
- This document standardizes pre-cutover readiness checks, telemetry contracts, launch gates, and a clear escalation matrix to reduce surprise rollbacks and disputes.

Scope:
- Applies to: enterprise tenant cutovers, major model version rollouts (e.g., gen-1 -> gen-2), quantization or architecture changes that affect response semantics, and high-risk routing changes (regional failover).
- Excludes: routine minor model config tweaks that are covered by auto-canary thresholds (see auto-canary spec).

Owners and roles:
- CS Owner: Aisha Patel — customer comms and consent
- Cutover Lead (SRE): Miguel Fernandez — orchestration, telemetry gating
- Product Lead: Emily Chen — model selection, rollback criteria
- Security/Compliance: Rajesh Kumar — data residency and KMS checks
- Billing/FinOps reviewer: Priya Menon — cost impact and SLA carveouts

Pre-cutover checklist (gates that must be green before customer-facing switch):
1) Telemetry contract signed (CS/SRE/Product) and baselines captured (see telemetry snippet).
2) Synthetic regression suite pass: latency, p99, token-per-request, and quality checks (at least 95% of prompt set within expected metric bands).
3) Observability enabled: tenant-level traces, sample output capture, and per-request model-id tagging.
4) Backout plan documented: automated switchback playbook, expected RTO (<= 5 mins) and RPO (<= 0 requests).
5) SLA carveout agreement noted for migration window (timeboxed with explicit credit formula).
6) Security & compliance signoff for any new network egress or KMS usage.

Telemetry contract (example JSON snippet to be checked in with cutover):
{
  "contract_version": "1.0",
  "signals": [
    {"name": "latency_p95_ms", "sampling": "100% request-level", "owner": "sre"},
    {"name": "token_rate_per_min", "sampling": "aggregate per-minute", "owner": "billing"},
    {"name": "semantic_regression_pct", "sampling": "per-prompt-suite daily", "owner": "product"},
    {"name": "kv_cache_hit_rate", "sampling": "1s sliding window", "owner": "runtime"}
  ],
  "retention": "90 days",
  "access": ["cs-team", "sre-oncall", "product"]
}

Minimum signal thresholds and actions (table):
| Signal | Threshold (migration baseline) | Immediate action if breached | Owner |
|---|---:|---|---|
| latency_p95_ms | <= 1200 ms | Abort migration, switchback within 5m | SRE |
| latency_p99_ms | <= 3000 ms | Trigger L2 paging and investigate | SRE/Product |
| semantic_regression_pct | <= 7% deviation vs baseline | Hold rollout, run extended evals | Product/CS |
| token_rate_per_min | < 3x expected | Auto-scale or throttle; notify FinOps | Runtime/FinOps |
| kv_cache_hit_rate | >= 60% | Proceed; if <40% abort and investigate cache warming | Runtime |

Cutover day runbook (high-level steps):
1. T-minus 4 hours: Finalize customer comms (scheduled window, expected impacts, on-call roster). CS sends templated notice (see Slack template below).
2. T-minus 2 hours: Run a full synthetic pass and upload results artifact to cutover ticket.
3. T-minus 30 minutes: Confirm telemetry contract live, sampling turned on, and retention set to 90 days.
4. T-minus 5 minutes: Set circuit-breaker thresholds to conservative values.
5. T0: Execute canary at 1% of traffic for 15 minutes. Monitor signals every minute.
6. T0 + 15m: If canary green, ramp to 10% for 20 minutes (automated step).
7. Progressive ramps: 10% -> 50% -> 100% with hold windows and explicit approvals from Cutover Lead.
8. Post-switch: Run end-to-end customer acceptance prompts and log outputs to the customer audit stream.

Rollback criteria (explicit, must be documented before T-minus 2h):
- Any threshold in "Immediate action" column breached.
- >10% of customer-critical prompt-suite failures in a 10-minute window.
- p99 latency > 2x baseline for 5 consecutive minutes.
- Unexpected increase in token billing estimate > 25% over projection for the hour.
If rollback is triggered: execute automated switchback, open an incident in the Incident Tracker, and initiate a post-mortem owner assignment within 24 hours.

Escalation matrix (who to page in order):
1) Cutover Lead (SRE) -> Miguel Fernandez (primary), paging channel: #sre-cutover-paging
2) Product (model quality) -> Emily Chen (primary)
3) CS escalation -> Aisha Patel (customer updates & acceptance)
4) Security -> Rajesh Kumar (if data-residency/KMS issues suspected)
5) FinOps -> Priya Menon (billing anomalies)
6) Exec on-call -> Engineering Director (if customer outage > 60 mins or material SLA dispute)

Slack templates (use before/after cutover):
- Pre-cutover notice (CS -> customer):
  Hi <customer-team>,
  We will start a scheduled model upgrade at <start-time UTC>. Expected user-visible changes: 
  - latency: +/- small variance
  - improved semantic accuracy for X prompts
  We expect a <duration> window; if you observe regressions after <T+30m> please open a support ticket and we will prioritize.

- Internal rapid update (SRE -> stakeholders):
  Cutover update: stage=<canary|ramp|complete|rollback>, traffic=<percent>, key_signals={latency_p95: 420ms, semantic_regression: 1.2%}. Next decision in 10m.

Post-cutover validation checklist (within 24h):
- Confirm autoscaling behaved as expected and no abnormal token spikes.
- Confirm synthetic regression suite still within expectations.
- Execute run of customer-critical prompts and collect adjudicated pass/fail.
- Prepare a short runbook for customer-facing operational quirks observed.
- Schedule QBR slot to review migration metrics and SLA carveouts if any.

SLA carveout template (example language):
- Time window: <start> to <end> (migration window)
- Carveout scope: latency and availability credit eligibility paused for customer-impact incidents directly caused by model semantic regressions discovered during the window (requires documented trial and rollback attempts).
- Credit formula: prorated daily uptime * 0.5 for migration window if rollback executed; otherwise standard credit rules apply. Decisions require signoff from CS + FinOps.

Dispute resolution steps (if customer rejects migration outcome):
1. CS collects adjudicated evidence: sampled outputs, synthetic suite results, and telemetry.
2. Convene 3-way review (CS/Product/SRE) within 48 hours to attempt remediation or offer rollback.
3. If unresolved, escalate to Legal & Finance for SLA credit arbitration.

Postmortem and QBR integration:
- Any migration with rollback or with a carveout invoked must produce a 1-page incident summary and a 45-minute QBR deep-dive within the next quarterly QBR cycle.
- Include the following QBR artifacts: baseline vs actual telemetry charts, adjudicated prompt examples, cost delta analysis, and customer sentiment summary.

Appendix A: Example queries to validate telemetry (CLI):
# p95 latency for tenant-123 in last 15m
redwood metrics query --tenant tenant-123 --metric latency_p95_ms --range 15m

# sample output capture for 10 requests containing prompt-set id 987
redwood audit fetch --tenant tenant-123 --prompt-set 987 --limit 10 --output sample.json

Appendix B: Sample automated canary policy (YAML):
policy:
  name: model-migration-canary
  steps:
    - percent: 1
      duration: 15m
      pass_criteria:
        latency_p95_ms: <1200
        semantic_regression_pct: <7
    - percent: 10
      duration: 20m
      approval: cutover_lead
    - percent: 50
      duration: 10m
      approval: cs_owner

Appendix C: Contacts and paging channels:
- SRE Cutover: miguel.fernandez@redwood.ai, slack: @miguel_f (channel #sre-cutover-paging)
- Product: emily.chen@redwood.ai, slack: @emily_c
- CS: aisha.patel@redwood.ai, slack: @aisha_p
- Security: rajesh.kumar@redwood.ai, slack: @rajesh_k
- FinOps: priya.menon@redwood.ai, slack: @priya_m

Notes and caveats:
- This playbook does not replace the dedicated security acceptance checklist for Private deployments; for Private, ensure on-prem KMS rotation and IP whitelists are validated at T-minus 24h.
- For very high-sensitivity customers (PHI/PCI), migrations require a dry-run in a mirrored staging environment with customer observers and explicit legal signoff.

Revision history:
- 2026-11-15: Created by Aisha Patel (initial draft)
- 2026-12-10: Added telemetry contract template and rollback thresholds (review: Miguel Fernandez)
- 2027-01-10: Finalized SLA carveout wording and dispute workflow (review: Emily Chen, Rajesh Kumar)

End of document.
